78-31-03-000-803-F00Lower Hydraulic Actuator Removal ATA 78 · Task 000-803-F00

Task Description

8. Lower Hydraulic Actuator Removal (Figure 403)

A. General

(1) This task is for the removal of the lower hydraulic actuator. (2) There are three hydraulic actuators on each torque box of the left and right thrust reversers on an engine. (3) The upper hydraulic actuator is a locking actuator, the middle and lower hydraulic actuators are non-locking actuators.

B. References

Reference Title 27-81-00-040-801 Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation (P/B 201) 27-81-00-860-804 Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-808 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 29-21-00-000-802 Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal (P/B 201) 71-11-02-010-801-F00 Open the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201) 78-31-00-010-801-F00 Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection) (P/B 201) 78-31-00-040-802-F00 Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance (P/B 201) 78-31-03 (Continued) Reference Title 78-31-00-980-803-F00 Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure) (P/B 201)

G. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-017-F00 WARNING DO THE THRUST REVERSER DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE TO PREVENT THE OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSER. ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSE CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00. 78-31-03 SUBTASK 78-31-03-860-004-F00 WARNING RETRACT THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS AND DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE BEFORE YOU OPEN THE LEFT OR THE RIGHT THRUST REVERSER ON AN ENGINE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (2) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804. SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-033-F00 (3) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation, TASK 27-81-00-040-801. SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-018-F00 (4) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. (a) For Engine 1, System A. (b) For Engine 2, System B. SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-019-F00 (5) Do this task: Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal, TASK 29-21-00-000-802. SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-020-F00 (6) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-021-F00 (7) For Engine 1, open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01003 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER IND B 7 C01266 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-022-F00 (8) For Engine 2, open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01267 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK C 8 C01004 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER IND SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-015-F00 (9) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-012-F00 CAUTION DO NOT MANUALLY EXTEND THE INBOARD THRUST REVERSER SLEEVE MORE THAN 10 INCHES. MAKE SURE THAT THE SLEEVE DOES NOT TOUCH THE WING LEADING EDGE WHEN YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (10) Do these steps to expose the gimbal pins and to prepare for the use of the actuator removal and installation tool: NOTE: The thrust reverser sleeve must be extended to remove the gimbal pins from the aft side of the torque box and to use the actuator removal and installation tool. 78-31-03 (a) For the inboard thrust reverser sleeve, do these steps to manually extend the thrust reverser sleeve: 1) Manually extend the thrust reverser sleeve no more than 10 in. (254 mm) from the forward edge of the torque box. a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00. (b) For the outboard thrust reverser sleeve, manually extend the thrust reverser sleeve to the fully extended position. NOTE: The outboard thrust reverser sleeve will not touch the leading edge of the wing and if the sleeve is fully extended, the tool will be easier to use. 1) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-019-F00 WARNING DO NOT INSTALL PRESSURE CAPS TO THE HYDRAULIC LINES THAT CONNECT TO CONTROL VALVE MODULE PORTS TO DEACTIVATE THE THRUST REVERSER. THE THRUST REVERSER CAN OPERATE WHEN PRESSURIZED. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHES AND GLOVES WHEN YOU DO WORK ON THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE A LEAK FROM THE OPEN PORTS OF THE COMPONENT OR FROM THE HYDRAULIC LINES. INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT LET HYDRAULIC FLUID GET ON THE THRUST REVERSER OR ENGINE COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN A COMPONENT IF HYDRAULIC FLUID GETS ON IT . HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT . CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO LOOSEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUT . USE ONE TO HOLD THE FITTING, AND THE OTHER TO LOOSEN THE COUPLING NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (11) Do these steps to drain the hydraulic fluid from the hydraulic lines (View B): NOTE: To decrease hydraulic fluid spray when the coupling nuts are loosened, wrap cotton wiper, G00034, around the wrench, nut and hydraulic line. (a) Wrap cotton wiper, G00034, around the electrical connector on the sync lock receptacle on the lower actuator. NOTE: The cloth will catch the hydraulic fluid and prevent damage to the electrical connector. (b) Loosen the two bolts on each of the two clampblocks that hold the lower hydraulic retract line [132]. NOTE: To remove the sleeve fitting on the hydraulic retract line from the actuator port, the hydraulic retract line must be carefully flexed. If the clampblocks are loose, the hydraulic retract line can be flexed easier. 78-31-03 (c) Disconnect the lower hydraulic retract line [132] at the lower actuator [103]. 1) Carefully remove the sleeve fitting on the lower hydraulic retract line [132] from the actuator port. 2) Let the hydraulic fluid drain in a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-1110. (d) Disconnect the coupling nut on the sync shaft tubing at the lower actuator [103]. 1) Let the hydraulic fluid drain into the 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-1110. 2) Move the coupling nut and tube adapter back along the tubing to get access to the sync shaft end. 3) Flex the sync shaft to remove it from the internal splined port in the lower actuator [103]. CAUTION DO NOT LET DIRT OR OTHER CONTAMINATION GET ON THE SYNC SHAFT . DAMAGE TO THE SYNC SHAFT CAN OCCUR. 4) Remove the sync shaft. a) Make sure that dirt or contamination does not get on the sync shaft. (e) Remove the union [110] and packing [111] from the upper retract port of the lower actuator (View B). 1) Keep the union [110] for the subsequent installation and discard the packing [111]. CAUTION USE ONLY HOLLOW CORE CAPS TO COVER THE ACTUATOR PORTS. IF YOU DO NOT , INTERNAL DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (f) Install protective covers on the hydraulic lines and actuator ports. SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-039-F00 (12) Do these steps to remove the sync lock [105]: (a) Disconnect the electrical connector from the sync lock receptacle (View B): 1) For the left thrust reverser, disconnect the electrical connector D1008. 2) For the right thrust reverser, disconnect the electrical connector D1016. (b) Remove the nut [106] and washer [107] from the adapter plug [108]. NOTE: You do not have to remove the two bolts that hold the bracket to the sync lock. After the coupling nut is loose, the bracket will move off the stud. (c) Loosen the coupling nut on the sync lock [105]. (d) Remove the sync lock [105] and bracket. (e) Remove the adapter plug [108] and packing [109]. 1) Discard the packing [109]. (f) Install protective covers on the sync lock [105] and lower actuator [103]. 78-31-03

H. Lower Actuator Removal

SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-040-F00 (1) Do these steps to remove the two gimbal pins [120] that attach the lower actuator [103] to the gimbal ring on the aft side of the torque box (View E): (a) If you use the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] to remove the gimbal pins [120], do these steps (View I): NOTE: Use a allen wrench, STD-7895 to turn the clamp block screws [40] and use a 1/4 inch allen wrench, STD-14286 to turn the adjustment screw [41]. 1) If not already done, loosen the clamp block screws [40] sufficiently so that the clamp block will fit over the lower actuator [103]. 2) Make sure that the adjustment screw [41] is retracted. NOTE: The adjustment screw is on the forward end of the tool. 3) Tilt the aft end of the clamp assembly tool down and over the aft cascade support ring. 4) Lower the forward end of the clamp assembly tool until the clamp block engages the lower actuator [103]. 5) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to move the clamp block aft. a) Move the clamp block until the aft edge touches where the diameter of the lower actuator [103] increases. 6) Tighten the clamp block screws [40]. 7) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to compress the fire seal [123] against the torque box. (b) Remove a bolt [121] and washer [122] from each of the two gimbal pins [120]. 1) Remove the two gimbal pins [120]. (c) If the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] was used, loosen the adjustment screw [41] and clamp block screws [40] to remove the tool. SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-011-F00 (2) Do these steps to remove the access door [116] and disconnect the rod end of the lower actuator [103] (View D): (a) To remove the applicable access doors [116], remove the nine bolts [115]. Number Name/Location 415FL Left Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 1 416FR Right Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 1 425FL Left Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 2 426FR Right Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 2 (b) Remove the nut [118], bolt [112], washer [113], washer [117], and bushing [114] that attach the rod end to the actuator attach fitting on the sleeve. 78-31-03 SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-016-F00 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU FULLY RETRACT THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS. MONITOR THE POSITION OF THE OPEN INBOARD THRUST REVERSER. THE THRUST REVERSER CAN TOUCH THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (3) Do these steps to get the necessary clearance to remove the lower actuator [103]: (a) For the inboard thrust reverser, do these steps to open the thrust reverser: 1) Make sure that the leading edge flaps are completely retracted. NOTE: Without hydraulics to hold the flaps in the retract position, the weight of the flaps can cause them to extend a small amount. 2) Monitor the position of the thrust reverser as it is opened to make sure that it does not touch the leading edge of the wing. 3) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00. (b) For the outboard thrust reverser, open the thrust reverser, do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00. NOTE: The outboard thrust reverser will not touch the leading edge of the wing. SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-012-F00 CAUTION WHEN YOU INSTALL THE LOWER ACTUATOR, YOU WILL MOVE THE PUSH ROD THOUGH AN OPENING IN THE TORQUE BOX AND THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING. DO NOT LET THE PUSH ROD HIT THE TORQUE BOX OR THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING, DAMAGE TO THE PUSH ROD CAN OCCUR. (4) Carefully remove the lower actuator [103]. SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-022-F00 (5) After you remove the lower actuator [103], do these steps: (a) Remove the fire shield [124] and the fire seal [123] from the lower actuator (View F). 1) Examine the fire seal [123] for damage. 2) If you find no damage, keep the fire seal for the subsequent installation. 3) If you find damage, replace the fire seal [123].

H. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-011-F00 (1) Do these steps to install the fire seal [123] and fire shield [124] on the lower actuator [103] (View F): (a) Put the fire seal [123] in the fire shield [124]. (b) Put the fire seal [123] and fire shield [124] over the rod end of the lower actuator [103]. 1) Make sure that the fire seal [123] will contact the forward side of the torque box.

I. Install the Lower Hydraulic Actuator

SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-012-F00 CAUTION WHEN YOU INSTALL THE LOWER ACTUATOR, YOU WILL MOVE THE PUSH ROD THOUGH AN OPENING IN THE TORQUE BOX AND THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING. DO NOT LET THE PUSH ROD HIT THE TORQUE BOX OR THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING, DAMAGE TO THE PUSH ROD CAN OCCUR. (1) Do these steps to install the lower actuator [103]: NOTE: Recommended to not turn the actuator rod end. For actuators without an Linear Variable Differential Transformer (LVDT), accidental rotation of the rod end will not cause detrimental effects. (a) To extend the rod end of the lower actuator [103], pull the rod end out by hand: NOTE: Do not let the rod end turn when you extend it manually. Make sure that you hold the rod end when you extend the actuator manually. Do not use hydraulic power to extend the rod end. NOTE: If necessary, thread a rag through the rod end bushing to provide grip as an aid during extension. Make sure you do not let the rod end turn. 1) For the inboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 10 in. (254 mm). 2) For the outboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 21 in. (533 mm). (b) Carefully insert the rod end through the opening in the torque box and aft cascade support ring. SUBTASK 78-31-03-860-005-F00 WARNING OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE PROCEDURE TO CLOSE THE THRUST REVERSERS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (2) Do this task: Close the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-804-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-013-F00 (3) Do these steps to install the two gimbal pins [120] that attach the lower actuator [103] to the gimbal ring on the aft side of the torque box (View E): (a) Apply grease, D00633 on the shanks of the two gimbal pins [120]. (b) Align the attachment holes in the lower actuator [103] and the gimbal ring. 78-31-03 (c) If you use the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] to compress the fire seal [123] against the torque box, do these steps (View I): NOTE: Use a 1/4-inch allen wrench to turn the adjustment screw and use a 3/16-inch allen wrench to turn the clamp block screws. 1) If not already done, loosen the clamp block screws [40] sufficiently, so that the clamp block will fit over the lower actuator [103]. 2) Make sure that the adjustment screw [41] is retracted. NOTE: The adjustment screw is on the forward end of the tool. 3) Tilt the aft end of the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] down and over the aft cascade support ring. 4) Lower the forward end of the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] until the clamp block engages the lower actuator [103]. 5) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to move the clamp block aft. a) Move the clamp block until the aft edge touches where the diameter of the lower actuator [103] increases. 6) Tighten the clamp block screws [40]. 7) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to compress the fire seal [123] against the torque box. 8) Turn the housing one direction or the other to align the attachment holes. (d) To manually compress the fire seal [123] against the torque box, do these steps: 1) Push aft on the forward end of the lower actuator [103] to compress the fire seal [123] against the torque box. 2) Turn the housing one direction or the other to align the attachment holes. (e) Install the two gimbal pins [120]. (f) Install a washer [122] and bolt [121] in each of the gimbal pins [120]. 1) Tighten the bolts [121] to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). (g) If the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] was used, loosen the adjustment screw [41] and clamp block screws [40] to remove the tool. SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-025-F00 (4) Align the rod end of the lower actuator [103] with the clevis on the attach fitting (View D). RYR 177-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-377; RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-176, 378-999 POST SB 737-78-1083; AIRPLANES WITH BONDED FITTING WEAR SPACER (a) Make sure the actuator attach fitting has a wear spacer [43] installed (Figure 403). 1) If a wear spacer [43] is not installed: a) Attach a wear spacer [43] into place with sealant, A00803. b) Seal around the edge of the fitting and inner sleeve. RYR ALL (b) Install the bushing [114], washer [113], washer [117], bolt [112], and nut [118] that attach the rod end. 1) Tighten the nut [118] to 370 in-lb (42 N·m) to 690 in-lb (78 N·m). 78-31-03 SUBTASK 78-31-03-410-014-F00 (5) Put the applicable access doors [116] in the correct position to align the bolt holes. Number Name/Location 415FL Left Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 1 416FR Right Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 1 425FL Left Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 2 426FR Right Thrust Reverser Actuator (Lower), Engine 2 (a) Install the nine bolts [115] to attach the access door [116]. 1) Tighten the bolts [115] to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) to 50 in-lb (6 N·m). SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-033-F00 (6) Do these steps if the replacement lower actuator [103] does not have the union [110] installed (View B): (a) Remove the protective covers from the lower actuator ports. (b) Lubricate a packing [111] with hydraulic fluid, D00153 or MCS 352B fluid, D00054. (c) Install the packing [111] on the union [110]. (d) Lubricate the threads of the union [110] with hydraulic fluid, D00153 or MCS 352B fluid, D00054. (e) Install the union [110] in the upper retract port. 1) Tighten the union [110] to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) to 283 in-lb (32 N·m). NOTE: Do not torque, loosen, then torque again (double-torque) a fitting that has a packing. SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-015-F00 (7) Do these steps to install the sync lock [105] and the adapter plug [108] (View B): (a) Lubricate a packing [109] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054. (b) Install the packing [109] on the adapter plug [108]. (c) Lubricate the threads of the adapter plug [108] with hydraulic fluid, D00153 or MCS 352B fluid, D00054. (d) Install the adapter plug [108] in the lower retract port of the lower actuator. 1) Tighten the adapter plug [108] to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) to 283 in-lb (32 N·m). NOTE: Do not torque, loosen, then torque again (double-torque) a fitting that has a packing. (e) Put the sync lock [105] in the correct position. 1) Make sure that the fastener hole in the bracket aligns with the stud on the adapter plug [108]. (f) Hand tighten the coupling nut on the sync lock [105]. (g) Install the washer [107] and nut [106] that connect the bracket to the adapter plug stud. 1) Tighten the nut [106] to 65 in-lb (7 N·m) to 100 in-lb (11 N·m). CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO TIGHTEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUT . USE ONE TO HOLD THE SYNC LOCK, AND THE OTHER TO TIGHTEN THE COUPLING NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (h) Tighten the coupling nut on the sync lock [105]. 78-31-03 1) Tighten the coupling nut to 855 in-lb (97 N·m) to 945 in-lb (107 N·m). 2) Loosen the coupling nut. 3) Tighten the coupling nut again to 855 in-lb (97 N·m) to 945 in-lb (107 N·m). SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-024-F00 (8) Do these steps to connect and tighten the hydraulic lines (View B): (a) Remove the protective covers from the hydraulic lines. (b) Connect the lower hydraulic retract line [132] to the upper retract port of the lower actuator [103]. 1) Hand tighten the coupling nut at this time. (c) Tighten the two bolts on each of the two clamp blocks that hold the lower hydraulic retract line [132]. 1) Tighten the bolts to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). (d) Tighten the coupling nut on the lower hydraulic retract line [132]. 1) Tighten the coupling nut to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) to 283 in-lb (32 N·m). 2) Loosen the coupling nut. 3) Tighten the coupling nut again 256 in-lb (29 N·m) to 283 in-lb (32 N·m). (e) Do these steps to temporarily install the lower sync shaft and tubing: NOTE: To manually retract the thrust reverser, the sync shafts must be temporarily installed. 1) Do this task: Sync Shaft - Inspection/Check, TASK 78-31-04-200-801-F00. 2) If there is contamination, remove the contamination from the sync shaft with a cotton wiper, G00034. 3) Move the coupling nut and tube adaptors along the tubing. 4) Insert the sync shaft into the tubing. a) Make sure that the sync shaft engages the internal spline in the middle actuator port. 5) Flex the sync shaft and insert the opposite end into the internal spline in the lower actuator port. 6) Tighten the coupling nut 855 in-lb (97 N·m) to 945 in-lb (107 N·m). NOTE: This is a temporary installation and it is not necessary to double-torque the coupling nuts. SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-014-F00 (9) Connect the electrical connectors to the sync lock receptacle (View B): (a) For the left thrust reverser, connect the electrical connector, D1008. (b) For the right thrust reverser, connect the electrical connector, D1016. SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-015-F00 (10) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Manual Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-804-F00. 78-31-03 SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-026-F00 WARNING DO ALL OF THE STEPS AND OBEY ALL OF THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS IN THE REFERENCED PROCEDURE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS WARNING, INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (11) To correctly rig the lower sync shaft between the lower actuator [103] and the middle actuator [51], do this step: (a) Do the reference tasks to remove and re-install the lower sync shaft that you temporarily installed. 1) Do this task: Sync Shaft Removal, TASK 78-31-04-000-801-F00. 2) Do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00. a) Make sure that the thrust reverser is completely retracted when rigging the sync shafts. NOTE: This task uses the thrust reverser maintenance lock equipment, SPL-9002. There are two -5 wire bundle cable assemblies in the B78009 tool assembly. SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-029-F00 (12) For Engine 1, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01003 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER IND B 7 C01266 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK SUBTASK 78-31-03-040-030-F00 (13) For Engine 2, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01267 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK C 8 C01004 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER IND SUBTASK 78-31-03-710-003-F00 WARNING DO ALL OF THE STEPS AND OBEY ALL OF THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS IN THE REFERENCED PROCEDURE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS WARNING, INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (14) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Normal Operation Test, TASK 78-31-00-700-801-F00. (a) Operate the thrust reverser through the deploy and stow cycles at least 3 times until the sleeves move smoothly. (b) Examine the thrust reverser area for hydraulic fluid leaks. 1) If you find leaks, do this task: Hydraulic System External Leakage Check, TASK 29-00-00-790-801. NOTE: Refer to the Tube Connections, Static Seals, and Other Dynamic Seals sections of the procedure for the leakage limits. SUBTASK 78-31-03-710-005-F00 (15) Do this task: Sync Lock Operational Test, TASK 78-31-00-700-803-F00. 78-31-03

THE ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSER CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Make sure that the thrust reversers are deactivated (TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00). E. Manual Lockout Handle Assembly Removal

SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-045-F00 (1) Do these steps to remove the manual unlock handle assembly [1]: (a) Mark the position of the handle relative to the actuator housing so that the manual unlock handle assembly is installed in the same position. (b) Remove the two screws [8] that attach the detent housing [7] to the actuator housing [11]. 78-31-03 (c) Remove the detent housing [7], manual unlock pin [6], spring [5] and spring guide [4]. (d) Remove the nut [9] from the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. (e) Remove the shim [10], unlock lever [3], torsion spring [2] and manual unlock handle assembly [1]. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove bushing [12] and bushing [13] on each side of the actuator housing [11].

E. Manual Lockout Handle Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-034-F00 (1) Do these steps to install the manual unlock handle assembly [1]: (a) Install the torsion spring [2] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. 1) Install one leg of the torsion spring [2] in the hole on the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. (b) Install the unlock lever [3] in the locked position in the actuator housing [11] (Figure 404) (Sheet 5). (c) Align the manual unlock handle assembly [1] with the mark (locked position) and insert the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through the bushing [13] until the splines just engage. 1) Pull the free leg of the torsion spring [2] around to align with the hole in the actuator housing [11]. 2) Push the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through until it bottoms on the bushing [13]. 3) Make sure that the torsion spring [2] is installed correctly. (d) Install the shim [10] with the counterbore towards the actuator housing [11]. (e) Install and tighten the nut [9] to 20 in-lb (2 N·m) - 30 in-lb (3 N·m). (f) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position. 78-31-03 (g) Make sure that the unlock lever [3] and manual unlock handle assembly [1] operate correctly with no binding. (h) Release the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back to the locked position. (i) Make sure that the actuator is in the stowed and locked position. 1) If not done, remove the nine bolts [14] from the access panel cover [15]. 2) If not done, remove the access panel cover [15] from the TR sleeve [19] to get access to the actuator rod end [18]. 3) Make sure that the gland nut [17] is within 0.007 in. (0.18 mm) - 0.033 in. (0.84 mm) of the rod stop [16]. (j) Do these steps to install the detent housing [7]: 1) Install the spring guide [4], spring [5], manual unlock pin [6] and detent housing [7] in the actuator housing [11]. 2) Install the two screws [8] that attach the detent housing [7] to the actuator housing [11]. 3) Tighten the two screws [8] to 27 in-lb (3.05 N·m) - 30 in-lb (3.39 N·m). 4) Install MS20995NC20 lockwire, G02166 to the two screws [8] (TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00). (k) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position, then push and release the manual unlock pin [6]. 1) Make sure that the manual unlock pin [6] does not bind and springs back smoothly. (l) Put the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back to the locked position. (m) Make sure that the actuator is in the stowed and locked position. 1) Look through the access area and see if the rod stop [16] rubs with the gland nut [17]. (n) Do this task: Torsion Spring Functional Check, TASK 78-31-03-700-802-F00. F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 78-31-03-410-020-F00 (1) Install the access panel cover [15] on the TR sleeve [19] with nine bolts [14]. SUBTASK 78-31-03-410-021-F00 (2) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-440-004-F00 (3) Do this task:Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-710-007-F00 (4) Do these checks: WARNING OBEY ALL OF THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS IN THE REFERENCED PROCEDURE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Normal Operation Test, TASK 78-31-00-700-801-F00. 1) Operate the thrust reverser through the deploy and stow cycles until the sleeves move smoothly. 78-31-03 2) Examine the thrust reverser area for hydraulic fluid leaks. (b) Do this task: EEC TEST , TASK 73-21-00-700-804-F00. NOTE: This check will make sure that the electrical connections for the LVDT's are correct. 1) Make sure that no Linear Variable Differential Transducer (LVDT) maintenance messages show. a) If a maintenance message shows, do the applicable fault isolation task in the Fault Isolation Manual for that maintenance message. b) If no maintenance messages show, the electrical connections for the LVDT are correct.

78-31-03-700-801-F00Thrust Reverser Upper Locking Actuator - Integrity Test ATA 78 · Task 700-801-F00

Task Description

1. Thrust Reverser Upper Locking Actuator - Integrity Test NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task is used to make sure that the locking actuator is properly functioning. (2) To engage the manual drive shaft in the sync lock [4], the lock release pin [3] in the 3/8 inch square opening [2] at the end of the sync lock [4] must be pushed in. (3) The sync lock [4] is connected to the lower hydraulic actuator, on the torque box. (4) A training video is available in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) supplements to assist with this task.

B. References

Reference Title 71-11-02-010-801-F00 Open the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201) 71-11-02-410-801-F00 Close the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201) 78-31-00-040-802-F00 Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance (P/B 201) 78-31-00-440-803-F00 Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance (P/B 201) 78-31-00-700-801-F00 Thrust Reverser Normal Operation Test (P/B 501) 78-31-00-980-801-F00 Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Selection) (P/B 201) 78-31-00-980-802-F00 Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Selection) (P/B 201) 78-31-00-980-806-F00 Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Power Procedure) (P/B 201) 78-31-03-000-801-F00 Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal (P/B 401) 78-31-03-400-801-F00 Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation (P/B 401)

C. Tools/Equipment

Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. This will make sure that the manual isolation valve handle on the control valve module is pinned in bypass mode. SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-018-F00 (2) Open these access panels: (TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00) Number Name/Location 413 Left Fan Cowl, Engine 1 414 Right Fan Cowl, Engine 1 423 Left Fan Cowl, Engine 2 424 Right Fan Cowl, Engine 2 SUBTASK 78-31-03-410-017-F00 (3) Make sure that these access panels are closed: Number Name/Location 521AB Outboard Leading Edge Blowout Door 521BB Outboard Lower Fixed Leading Edge Access Panel 621AB Outboard Leading Edge Blowout Door 621BB Outboard Lower Fixed Leading Edge Access Panel 78-31-03

G. Thrust Reverser Upper Locking Actuator - Integrity Test

SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-013-F00 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE AREA AFT OF THE APPLICABLE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION STOP THE MANUAL EXTENSION IF THE THRUST REVERSER EXTENDS AT AN ANGLE. THIS IS AN INDICATION THAT THERE ARE SYNC SHAFTS THAT ARE BROKEN OR NOT INSTALLED. IF YOU CONTINUE, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 50 INCH-POUNDS OF TORQUE TO EXTEND OR RETRACT THE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO, DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT ENGAGE THE MANUAL UNLOCK PIN ON THE UPPER LOCKING HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR BY PREVIOUS MAINTENANCE ACTIONS. THIS WILL PREVENT THE COMPLETION OF THE INTEGRITY TEST . IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THIS CAUTION, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE THRUST REVERSER SLEEVE DOES NOT HIT THE WING IF THE THRUST REVERSER IS IN THE 45-DEGREE OPEN POSITION. DO NOT EXTEND THE INBOARD SLEEVE. DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Obey all of these WARNINGS and CAUTIONS when you do this procedure. SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-016-F00 (2) Do these steps to release the lock for the upper actuator with the manual unlock handle (Figure 501): (a) Move the manual unlock lever forward. (b) Hold the manual unlock lever in the forward position as you push the detent pin in. (c) Release the manual unlock lever. SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-014-F00 CAUTION DO NOT HIT THE END OF THE SYNC LOCK OR THE 3/8 INCH DRIVE WRENCH TO PUSH THE LOCK RELEASE PIN. DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR. (3) Do these steps to unlock sync lock [4], engage manual drive, and to manually extend the thrust reverser (Figure 502): (a) For the standard hand tools: 1) Put a 3/8 inch square drive speed wrench, STD-997, or equivalent into the 3/8 inch square opening [2]. NOTE: The 3/8 drive wrench will go into the opening approximately 0.30 in. (7.62 mm). 78-31-03 2) Apply pressure until the lock release pin [3] goes in. 3) Use a standard wrench, STD-6760, or equivalent on the hex nut [1] at the end of the sync lock [4] and slowly move a small amount, in one direction and then the other, to help the lock release pin [3] go in. NOTE: The open ended wrench is only needed to assist the 3/8 square-drive to go in. (b) For the fully depressed drive socket, SPL-18641: 1) Put a 3/8 inch square drive speed wrench, STD-997, or equivalent into the 3/8-inch square opening in the drive socket. NOTE: The 3/8 drive wrench will go into the opening approximately 0.30 in. (7.62 mm). 2) Mate the socket with the hex nut [1] on the end of the sync lock [4]. 3) Apply pressure until the lock release pin [3] goes in. 4) Move the fully depressed drive socket, SPL-18641, a small amount in one direction and then the other, to help the lock release pin [3] go in. CAUTION WHILE YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER, APPLY CONTINUOUS PRESSURE ON THE LOCK RELEASE PIN WITH THE SQUARE-DRIVE WRENCH. THIS MAKES SURE THAT THE LOCK RELEASE PIN IS PUSHED IN. THIS WILL KEEP THE MANUAL DRIVE FULLY ENGAGED. IF YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER AND YOU DO NOT FULLY ENGAGE THE MANUAL DRIVE, DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR. (c) From the fully stowed position of the thrust reverser sleeve, manually extend the thrust reverser by gradually applying a continuous torque of up to 50 in-lb (6 N·m). 1) To extend the right reverser sleeve, turn the wrench clockwise. 2) To extend the left thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench counter clockwise. (d) If the thrust reverser is in the 45-degree open position, do these steps: 1) For the inboard thrust reverser sleeve, do these steps: a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps are fully retracted. b) Monitor the position of the thrust reverser sleeve. <1> Make sure that it does not touch the wing. (e) Make sure that the thrust reverser sleeves operate smoothly. NOTE: Thrust reverser needs to be extended at least 10 in. (254 mm) from the fully stowed position. SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-017-F00 CAUTION DO NOT HIT THE END OF THE SYNC LOCK OR THE 3/8 INCH DRIVE WRENCH TO PUSH THE LOCK RELEASE PIN. DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR. (4) Do these steps to retract the thrust reverser (Figure 502): 78-31-03 CAUTION AS YOU RETRACT THE THRUST REVERSER, APPLY CONTINUOUS PRESSURE ON THE LOCK RELEASE PIN WITH THE SQUARE DRIVE WRENCH TO KEEP THE LOCK RELEASE PIN PUSHED IN. THIS WILL KEEP THE MANUAL DRIVE FULLY ENGAGED. IF YOU RETRACT THE THRUST REVERSER WHEN THE MANUAL DRIVE IS NOT FULLY ENGAGED, DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR. (a) To retract the left thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench clockwise. (b) To retract the right thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench counterclockwise. NOTE: The sleeve will be at the manual track limit when you hear the override clutch on the manual drive make a "ratcheting" sound. If the locking actuator has not locked at this time, hydraulic power will be necessary to completely retract and lock the thrust reverser. 1) If it is necessary to use hydraulic power to completely retract and lock the thrust reverser, then do these steps: a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00. b) Do the applicable steps in this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Power Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-806-F00. c) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00. (c) Make sure that the thrust reverser sleeves operate smoothly. (d) Make sure that manual drive unit is turned until the thrust reverser sleeves are fully retracted. (e) Put the upper locking actuator to the locked position with the manual unlock handle. SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-018-F00 (5) Do these steps to make sure that thrust reverser upper locking actuator operates correctly. (a) Make sure that the upper actuator with the manual unlock is locked. NOTE: To completely retract and lock the thrust reverser, it can be necessary to use hydraulic power. You can use a wrench to partially retract the thrust reverser, however if the locking actuator does not lock, hydraulic power will be necessary to completely retract and lock the thrust reverser. CAUTION WHILE YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER, APPLY CONTINUOUS PRESSURE ON THE LOCK RELEASE PIN WITH THE SQUARE-DRIVE WRENCH. THIS MAKES SURE THAT THE LOCK RELEASE PIN IS PUSHED IN. THIS WILL KEEP THE MANUAL DRIVE FULLY ENGAGED. IF YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER AND YOU DO NOT FULLY ENGAGE THE MANUAL DRIVE, DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR. (b) From the fully stowed position of the thrust reverser sleeve, try to manually extend the thrust reverser by gradually applying a continuous torque of up to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) or until you hear the override clutch on the sync lock manual drive making the “ratcheting” sound. 1) To extend the right reverser sleeve, turn the wrench clockwise. 2) To extend the left thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench counter clockwise. (c) If the thrust reverser is in the 45-degree open position, do these steps: 78-31-03 1) For the inboard thrust reverser sleeve, do these steps: a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps are fully retracted. b) Monitor the position of the thrust reverser sleeve. <1> If it extends, make sure that it does not touch the wing. (d) Make sure that the thrust reverser does not deploy. NOTE: If the thrust reverser sleeve stays in the fully stowed position, the thrust reverser upper locking actuator is serviceable. NOTE: Some movement of the thrust reverser sleeve can occur near the lower hydraulic actuator. This is because of the wind up in the flexible shafts between the sync lock and the lock of the upper locking hydraulic actuator. (e) Stop manual deployment, if the thrust reverser sleeve starts to deploy. NOTE: If a thrust reverser sleeve can be manually translated, the upper locking hydraulic actuator is not serviceable. 1) Replace the upper locking hydraulic actuator before the next flight, do these tasks: a) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00, b) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE TORQUE ON THE SYNC LOCK IS AT ZERO BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE SQUARE-DRIVE WRENCH. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THERE IS A POSSIBILITY THAT THE THRUST REVERSER CANNOT DEPLOY WHEN COMMANDED AND DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (f) Remove the square-drive wrench or fully depressed drive socket, SPL-18641, from the sync lock [4]. (g) Make sure that the sync lock release pin [3] does not stay in the pushed in condition, after the square-drive wrench is removed.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 78-31-03-840-002-F00 (1) Close these access panels: (TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00) Number Name/Location 413 Left Fan Cowl, Engine 1 414 Right Fan Cowl, Engine 1 423 Left Fan Cowl, Engine 2 424 Right Fan Cowl, Engine 2 SUBTASK 78-31-03-440-003-F00 (2) Do one of the following: 78-31-03 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO AN INSPECTION FOR FAULTS AFTER THE THRUST REVERSER ACTIVATION AND LOCK INTEGRITY TEST PROCEDURES. IF THERE ARE FAULTS, DO TROUBLESHOOTING. REFER TO THE 737-600/700/800/900 FIM 78-31. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THERE IS A POSSIBILITY THAT THE THRUST REVERSER CANNOT DEPLOY WHEN COMMANDED AND DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (a) Do a manual thrust reverser extension and retraction, do these tasks: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-980-801-F00 and Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-980-802-F00. 1) Activate the thrust reverser, do this task: Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO AN INSPECTION FOR FAULTS AFTER THE THRUST REVERSER ACTIVATION AND USUAL OPERATION CHECK PROCEDURES. IF THERE ARE FAULTS, DO TROUBLESHOOTING. REFER TO THE 737-600/700/800/900 FIM 78-31. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THERE IS A POSSIBILITY THAT THE THRUST REVERSER CANNOT DEPLOY WHEN COMMANDED AND DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (b) Activate the thrust reverser, do this task: Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00. 1) Do the thrust reverser normal operation check, do this task: Thrust Reverser Normal Operation Test, TASK 78-31-00-700-801-F00.

78-31-03-610-801-F00Thrust Reverser Hydraulic Actuator Rod End and Clevis Inspection ATA 78 · Task 610-801-F00

Task Description

2. Thrust Reverser Hydraulic Actuator Rod End and Clevis Inspection (Figure 601) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

G. Manual Unlock Handle Assembly Rigging

SUBTASK 78-31-03-820-001-F00 (1) Do these steps to align the manual unlock handle assembly [1]: (a) Install the torsion spring [8] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. 1) Install one leg of the torsion spring [8] in the hole on the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. (b) Install the unlock lever [7] in the locked position on the actuator housing [13] (Figure 602) (Sheet 5 or 6). (c) Align the manual unlock handle assembly [1] with the mark (locked position) and insert the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through the bushing [21] until the splines just engage. 1) Pull the free leg of the torsion spring [8] around to align it with the hole in the actuator housing [13]. 2) Push the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through until it bottoms on the bushing [21]. a) Make sure that the torsion spring [8] is installed correctly. (d) Install the shim [5] with the counterbore towards the actuator housing [13] (Figure 603). 1) Measure the gap G between the shim [5] and the bushing [20]. a) If gap G is more than 0.004 in. (0.102 mm), then make a new shim [5]. b) If there is no gap so that the shim [5] face is in contact with the bushing [20], then trim the shim [5]. <1> Measure F , the distance from the shoulder end of the lockout handle shaft, and subtract 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) from F to get the shim thickness (S3). <2> Trim the shim [5] face that makes contact with bushing [20] to obtain the S3 thickness (the gap tolerance is 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) - 0.004 in. (0.102 mm)). NOTE: A new shim [5] will be oversized. The new shim [5] face will be in contact with the bushing [20]. You will need to trim the new shim [5] to obtain the 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) gap. (e) Install and tighten nut [6] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m). (f) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position and release the manual unlock handle assembly [1] (Figure 605). 1) Make sure that the manual unlock handle assembly [1] moves back smoothly. (g) Make sure that the unlock lever [7] and manual unlock handle assembly [1] operate correctly with no binding. (h) Put the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back in the locked position. (i) Make sure that the actuator is in the stowed and locked position. 1) Remove the nine bolts [14] from the access panel cover [15]. 2) Remove access panel cover [15] from the TR sleeve [19] to get access to the actuator rod end [18]. 3) Make sure that the gland nut [17] is within 0.007 in. (0.18 mm) - 0.033 in. (0.84 mm) of the rod stop [16]. 78-31-03 (j) Do these steps to install the target [3] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1] (Figure 602 and Figure 604): NOTE: It is recommended to use the proximity sensor locator, SPL-4156, or gap gauge, SPL-13657, to put the target [3] in position on the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. 1) Apply and keep slight pressure to the manual unlock handle assembly [1] in the unlock position. NOTE: Keep light pressure against the internal lock sleeve but do not move the sleeve. CAUTION DO NOT USE A DISTANCE MORE THAN 0.37 INCHES (9.40 MM) BETWEEN THE TARGET [3] AND BRACKET SENSOR HOLE. IF YOU DO, IT COULD CAUSE AN INCORRECT LOCKED ACTUATOR INDICATION. 2) Make sure that the target [3] is 0.33 in. (8.38 mm) - 0.37 in. (9.40 mm) from the center of the bracket sensor hole. 3) T emporarily attach the target [3] to the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. 4) Remove the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. a) Remove the nut [6], shim [5], unlock lever [7] and torsion spring [8]. 5) Match drill to the target [3]. NOTE: This will align the holes on the target [3] and manual unlock handle assembly [1]. 6) Install the target [3] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1] with two rivets [4]. SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-037-F00 (2) Do this task: Manual Unlock Handle Assembly Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-805-F00.

E. Freeplay Check

SUBTASK 78-31-03-220-002-F00 (1) Do one of these procedures to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit is within limits: (a) Do these steps to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit: 1) From the locked position, move the manual unlock handle assembly [1] aft until it stops. 2) Use an angular measurement tool to measure the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play (Figure 605). 3) If the free-play is less than or equal to 9.40 degrees, continue with the procedure to replace the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. 4) If the free-play is more than 9.40 degrees, replace the actuator. Do these tasks: a) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00 b) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00. (b) Do these steps to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit with the free play gauge, SPL-18803 (C78042-23) (Figure 606 (Sheet 1)): 1) Install the gauge assembly on the upper locking hydraulic actuator. 2) Attach the gauge assembly to the actuator housing by inserting the index pin into the applicable hole in the actuator housing. a) Align the assembly to secure it to the actuator housing using captive screw. 78-31-03 3) Make sure that the slide cutout edge labeled "START" touches the unlock handle. NOTE: The unlock handle of the manual unlock handle assembly [1] should be in the forward stop position. a) If it is necessary, push the unlock handle lightly in the forward direction until it stops. b) Do not move the manual unlock handle. 4) With the slide in the adjusted position, tighten knob to secure gauge assembly. 5) Push the manual unlock handle aft until it stops. a) If the manual unlock handle touches the FAIL edge, replace the actuator. b) If the actuator needs to be replaced, do these tasks: <1> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00 <2> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00. (c) Do these steps to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit with the free play gauge, SPL-18803 (C78042-17) (Figure 606 (Sheet 2)): 1) Make sure that the correct side of the Go/Fail slide is used for each upper locking hydraulic actuator. NOTE: Each side of the Go/Fail slide is marked with the actuator part number(s) that it can be used with. 2) If an incorrect side of the tool faces the actuator, loosen the top knob to allow rotation of the Go/Fail slide, then hand tighten the top knob. 3) Install free play gauge, SPL-18803, onto the manual unlock handle side of the upper locking hydraulic actuator at the two threaded holes. a) The un-threaded pin slides into the top threaded hole closest to the manual unlock handle, the threaded knob screws into the bottom threaded hole. 4) Loosen the top knob and move the Go/Fail slide forward or aft until the GO edge makes contact with the manual unlock handle flange. a) When the Go/Fail slide is in position, tighten the top knob. b) Do not move the manual unlock handle. 5) Push the manual unlock handle aft until it stops. a) If the manual unlock handle makes contact with the FAIL edge, replace the actuator. b) If the actuator needs to be replaced, do these tasks: <1> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00 <2> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00. (d) Do the steps that follow to measure the manual unlock handle assembly free-play: 1) Measure the radial height by locating a point on the manual unlock handle assembly and measuring the distance from the handle axis to this point. A point from Table 601 can be used. 78-31-03 Table 601/78-31-03-993-803-F00 Suggested Radial Heights on Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Manual Unlock Handle Location Manual Unlock Handle Assembly Part Number 315A2801–1 Manual Unlock Handle Assembly Part Number 315A2801–4 OR 315A2801–5 Radial Height in Inches (Ref) Radial Height in Inches (Ref) Handle Tip 2.94 2.91 Upper Rivet 2.77 2.55 Lower Rivet 1.92 2.11 Sensor Center 2.15 2.15 2) Fix a pair of calipers in a location that allows for lateral measurement of that point parallel to the top of the sensor bracket. NOTE: The caliper tip can be pressed against the flat surface of the handle for ease. 3) If the calipers are set up opposite to that in Figure 605, zero the calipers when the manual unlock handle assembly is pushed in the forward direction, and measure the deflection when the manual unlock handle assembly is pushed aft. 4) Push the manual unlock handle assembly in the aft direction until it stops, then zero the calipers. 5) Measure the deflection by pressing lightly on the manual unlock handle assembly towards the forward direction until it stops. Do not unlock the actuator. 6) Make sure that the maximum deflection is not more than the values shown in Table 602 if the suggested radial heights in Table 601 are used. 7) If the measured deflection exceeds the values in Table 602, replace the actuator. Do these tasks: a) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00 b) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00. Zone Area 415 Engine 1 - Thrust Reverser, Left 416 Engine 1 - Thrust Reverser, Right 425 Engine 2 - Thrust Reverser, Left 426 Engine 2 - Thrust Reverser, Right F. Procedure SUBTASK 78-31-03-860-014-F00 (1) For on-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1], do these steps: WARNING DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE TO PREVENT THE OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSER. THE ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSER CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00. (b) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00. (c) Make sure the thrust reverser sleeve is in the stowed and locked position. SUBTASK 78-31-03-200-001-F00 (2) Do these steps to verify the lock handle freeplay limit is within limits: 78-31-03 (a) Measure and mark the measurement point on the locking actuator unlock handle denoted (X) in Figure 804. This point is 2.15 ±0.01 in. (54.61 ±0.25 mm) from the center of the handle axis of rotation. (b) Clamp or fix the dial indicator in a location that allows for lateral measurement of that point. NOTE: If the dial indicator is setup opposite to that in Figure 804, zero the dial indicator when the handle is pushed in the forward direction, and measure the deflection when the handle is pushed aft. (c) Push the unlock handle aft until it stops (1 st point). Zero the dial indicator. (d) Press lightly on the unlock handle towards the Forward direction until it stops (2 nd point). Do not unlock the actuator. (e) If the dial indicator reads less than or equal to 0.095 in. (2.413 mm), the Manual Unlock Handle Assembly Replacement may continue. (f) If this difference is greater than 0.095 in. (2.413 mm), replace the actuator. These are the tasks: 1) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00. 2) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-000-003-F00 (3) For off-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1]: (a) Do this task: Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00. (b) Retract and lock the actuator. SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-048-F00 (4) Do these steps to remove the defective manual unlock handle assembly [1]: (a) Mark the position of the handle relative to the actuator housing so that the new handle assembly is installed in the same position. 1) In the locked position, the handle lever is approximately vertical to the axis of the actuator. (b) Remove the two screws [9] that attach the detent housing [2] to the actuator housing [13]. (c) Remove the detent housing [2], manual unlock pin [10], spring [11], and spring guide [12]. (d) Remove the nut [6] from the manual unlock handle assembly [1]. (e) Remove the shim [5], unlock lever [7], torsion spring [8], and manual unlock handle assembly [1]. (f) Do not remove the two bushings. SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-038-F00 (5) Do these steps to install the new manual unlock handle assembly [1]: (a) Install the torsion spring [8] on the new manual unlock handle assembly [1]. 1) Locate one leg of the spring in the hole. (b) Install the unlock lever [7] in the locked position in the actuator housing [13] (Figure 801) (Sheet 3). (c) Align the manual unlock handle assembly [1] with the mark (locked position) and insert the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through the bushing until the splines just engage. 1) Pull the free leg of the torsion spring [8] around to align with the hole in the actuator housing [13]. 78-31-03 2) Push the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through until it bottoms on the bushing [21]. 3) Make sure the torsion spring [8] is installed correctly. (d) Install the shim [5] with the counterbore towards the actuator housing [13] (Figure 802). 1) Measure the gap G between the shim [5] and the bushing [20]. a) If the gap G is more than 0.004 in. (0.102 mm), make a new shim [5]. b) If there is no gap and the shim face is in contact with the bushing [20], shim [5] must be trimmed. <1> Measure F (the distance from the shoulder end of the unlock handle shaft) and subtract 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) to get S3 (the shim thickness). <2> Trim the shim face that contacts the bushing [20] to obtain the S3 thickness (the gap tolerance is 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) - 0.004 in. (0.102 mm). NOTE: A new shim is oversized. The shim face will be in contact with the bushing and requires trimming to obtain the 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) inch gap. (e) Install the nut [6] and tighten the nut to 20-30 inch-pounds (2.26-3.39 newton-meters): (f) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position and make sure the unlock lever [7] and manual unlock handle assembly [1] operate correctly with no binding. (g) Put the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back to the locked position and make sure the actuator is in the stowed and locked position. 1) Remove the nine bolts [14] from the access panel cover [15]. 2) Remove the access panel cover [15] on the TR sleeve [19] to get access to the actuator rod end [18]. 3) Make sure that the gland nut [17] is within 0.007-0.033 inch (0.1778-0.8382 mm) of the rod stop [16]. (h) Do these steps to install the detent housing [2]: 1) Install the spring guide [12], spring [11], manual unlock pin [10], and detent housing [2] in the actuator housing [13]. 2) Install the two screws [9] that attach the detent housing [2] to the actuator housing [13]. 3) Tighten the two screws [9] to 27-30 inch-pounds (3.05-3.39 newton-meters). 4) Install lockwire to the screws [9]. (i) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position, then push and release the manual unlock pin [10]. 1) Make sure there is no binding and the manual unlock pin [10] springs back smoothly. (j) Put the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back to the locked position and make sure the actuator is in the stowed and locked position. 1) Look through the access area and see if the rod stop [16] is in contact with the gland nut [17]. (k) Do these steps to install the target [3] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1] (Figure 803): 78-31-03 1) Use the proximity sensor locator, SPL-4156 or gap gauge, SPL-13657, to position the target [3] on the handle. 2) Apply and keep a slight pressure to the handle in the unlock position (light pressure against internal lock sleeve, but do not move sleeve). 3) The target [3] must be 0.33-0.37 inch (8.38-9.40 mm) from the center of the bracket sensor hole. NOTE: Do not exceed a distance greater than 0.37 inches (9.40 mm) between the target [3] and bracket sensor hole. It could lead to a false locked actuator indication. 4) Install the target [3] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1].

G. Put The Airplane Back To Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 78-31-03-410-022-F00 (1) For on-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1], do these steps: (a) Install the access panel cover [15] on the TR sleeve [19] with nine bolts [14]. (b) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00. (c) Do this task:Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-400-004-F00 (2) For off-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1]: (a) Do this task: Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-03-710-009-F00 (3) For on-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1], do these checks: WARNING OBEY ALL OF THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS IN THE REFERENCED PROCEDURE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Normal Operation Test, TASK 78-31-00-700-801-F00. 1) Operate the thrust reverser through the deploy and stow cycles until the sleeves move smoothly. 2) Examine the thrust reverser area for hydraulic fluid leaks. (b) Do this task: EEC TEST , TASK 73-21-00-700-804-F00. NOTE: This check will make sure that the electrical connections for the LVDT's are correct. 1) Make sure that no LVDT maintenance messages show. a) If a maintenance message shows, do the applicable fault isolation task in the Fault Isolation Manual for that maintenance message. b) If no maintenance messages show, the electrical connections for the LVDT are correct.

78-31-04-000-801-F00Sync Shaft Removal ATA 78 · Task 000-801-F00

Task Description

2. Sync Shaft Removal (Figure 401, Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This task is for the removal of the sync shafts from the left or right thrust reverser on an engine. (2) The sync shaft is between the upper and middle actuators and between the middle and lower actuators on each thrust reverser torque box.

B. References

Reference Title 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-808 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 71-11-02-010-801-F00 Open the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201) 78-31-00-040-802-F00 Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance (P/B 201)

E. Location Zones

Zone Area 415 Engine 1 - Thrust Reverser, Left 416 Engine 1 - Thrust Reverser, Right 425 Engine 2 - Thrust Reverser, Left 426 Engine 2 - Thrust Reverser, Right 78-31-04 F. Prepare for the Removal SUBTASK 78-31-04-040-001-F00 WARNING DO THE THRUST REVERSER DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE TO PREVENT THE OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSER. ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSE CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-001-F00 (2) For Engine 1, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 7 C01266 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-002-F00 (3) For Engine 2, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01267 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-003-F00 (4) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-004-F00 (5) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 78-31-04-010-001-F00 (6) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-020-001-F00 WARNING DO NOT INSTALL PRESSURE CAPS TO THE HYDRAULIC LINES THAT CONNECT TO CONTROL VALVE MODULE PORTS TO DEACTIVATE THE THRUST REVERSER. THE THRUST REVERSER CAN OPERATE WHEN PRESSURIZED. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHES AND GLOVES WHEN YOU DO WORK ON THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE A LEAK FROM THE OPEN PORTS OF THE COMPONENT OR FROM THE HYDRAULIC LINES. INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT LET HYDRAULIC FLUID GET ON THE THRUST REVERSER OR ENGINE COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN A COMPONENT IF HYDRAULIC FLUID GETS ON IT . HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT . 78-31-04 (CAUTION PRECEDES) CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO LOOSEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUT . USE ONE TO HOLD THE FITTING, AND THE OTHER TO LOOSEN THE COUPLING NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (7) Do these steps to drain the hydraulic fluid from the hydraulic lines: NOTE: To decrease hydraulic fluid spray when the coupling nuts are loosened, wrap cotton wiper, G00034, around the wrench, coupling nut and hydraulic line. (a) Wrap cotton wiper, G00034, around the electrical connector on the sync lock receptacle on the lower actuator. NOTE: The cloth will catch the hydraulic fluid and prevent contamination of the electrical connector. (b) Disconnect the sync shaft tubing at the lower actuator. (c) Disconnect the hydraulic retract line at the lower actuator. (d) Let the hydraulic fluid drain into a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-1110. (e) Loosen the coupling nuts on the extend line and retract line flexhoses at the upper actuator. NOTE: This will let air into the hydraulic lines to let the hydraulic fluid drain. SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-001-F00 (8) Tighten the coupling nut on the retract line flexhose at the upper actuator. (a) Tighten the coupling nut to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32.0 N·m). (b) Loosen the coupling nut. (c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32.0 N·m). SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-002-F00 (9) Tighten the coupling nut on the extend line flexhose at the upper actuator. (a) Tighten the coupling nut to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m). (b) Loosen the coupling nut. (c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m). SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-003-F00 (10) Re-connect the retract line at the lower actuator. (a) Tighten the coupling nut to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32.0 N·m). (b) Loosen the coupling nut. (c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32.0 N·m). SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-006-F00 (11) If the lower sync shaft will not be removed, re-connect the sync shaft tubing at the lower actuator. (a) Tighten the coupling nut to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m). (b) Loosen the coupling nut. (c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m). 78-31-04 SUBTASK 78-31-04-010-002-F00 (12) If the upper sync shaft and tubing will be removed, do this step to remove the upper clampblock [11]: (a) Remove the two bolts [9], two washers [10], clampblock retainer [8], and clampblock [11]. NOTE: To eliminate tubing preload, it is important to keep the clampblock retainer, clampblock, and spacers together and to note their position for the subsequent installation. SUBTASK 78-31-04-010-003-F00 (13) If the lower sync shaft and tubing will be removed, do this step to remove the lower clampblock [18]: (a) Remove the two bolts [16], two washers [17], clampblock retainer [15], and clampblock [18]. NOTE: To eliminate tubing preload, it is important to keep the clampblock retainer, clampblock, and spacers together and to note their position for the subsequent installation.

G. Sync Shaft Removal

SUBTASK 78-31-04-020-002-F00 CAUTION DO NOT LET DIRT OR OTHER CONTAMINATION GET ON THE SYNC SHAFT . DAMAGE TO THE SYNC SHAFT CAN OCCUR. (1) Do these steps to remove the upper or lower sync shaft [4]: (a) Disconnect the coupling nuts at the two ends of the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3]. (b) Move the coupling nuts and tube adapters back along the tube to get access to the sync shaft ends. (c) Flex the sync shaft [4] to remove it from the internal splined port in the actuator port [1]. (d) Remove the sync shaft [4] and tube [2] or tube [3] together. SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-004-F00 WARNING INSTALL THE TUBING TEMPORARILY WITHOUT THE SYNC SHAFT . IF YOU APPLY PRESSURE, THE TUBING WILL COLLECT THE HYDRAULIC FLUID. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (2) Do these steps to temporarily install the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3]: (a) Put the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3], without the sync shaft [4], in its position between the actuators. (b) Tighten the coupling nuts to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m). NOTE: This is a temporary installation and it is not necessary to tighten, loosen, then tighten again (double-torque) the coupling nuts.

78-31-04-400-801-F00Sync Shaft Installation ATA 78 · Task 400-801-F00

Task Description

3. Sync Shaft Installation (Figure 401, Figure 402)

A. General

(1) After you install the sync shaft and tubing, you must do the thrust reverser normal operational test. (2) To correctly rig the sync shaft, hydraulic pressure must be applied to the retract side of the thrust reverser actuators when the sync shaft is installed. (3) The upper and lower sync shafts are interchangeable and can be reversed end for end.

G. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 78-31-04-480-001-F00 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU DEACTIVATE THE DEPLOY CONTROL CIRCUIT . THIS WILL MAKE SURE THAT THE HYDRAULIC PRESSURE IS ON THE RETRACT LINE ONLY . IF YOU DO NOT , THE TR SLEEVES CAN DEPLOY . INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) To prevent the actuation of the deploy circuit, do these steps to connect the B78009-5 cable assembly from the thrust reverser maintenance lock equipment, SPL-9002, to the control valve module: NOTE: The B78009-5 cable assembly is part of the thrust reverser maintenance lock equipment. There are two -5 wire bundle cable assemblies in the B78009 tool. (a) Disconnect the electrical connector from the applicable control valve module receptacle. 1) For Engine 1, disconnect the electrical connector, D03052. 2) For Engine 2, disconnect the electrical connector, D03056. (b) Connect the P1 connector of the -5 cable assembly to the control valve module receptacle. (c) Connect the electrical connector to the J1 receptacle of the -5 cable assembly. SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-005-F00 (2) Do these steps to supply hydraulic power to the retract side of the actuators: (a) Make sure that the tube [2] and tube [3] are temporarily installed. (b) Move the applicable reverse thrust lever up and aft to the extend (deploy) position. NOTE: This will unlock the sync lock. 1) Install a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858. (c) For Engine 1, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 5 C00276 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER CONT B 7 C01266 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK (d) For Engine 2, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01267 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK C 7 C00277 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER CONT WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THE AILERONS, RUDDER, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (e) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. 1) For Engine 1, pressurize hydraulic system A. 2) For Engine 2, pressurize hydraulic system B. 78-31-04 (f) Make sure that the reverse thrust lever is up and aft in the extend (deploy) position. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU PARTIALLY DEPLOY THE THRUST REVERSER, IT WILL RETRACT WHEN YOU REMOVE THE LOCKPIN. INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (g) Remove the lockpin from the manual isolation valve handle on the control valve module. NOTE: Because the cable assembly is installed that disables the deploy actuation circuit, the thrust reverser will retract (stow) as soon as the lockpin is removed from the manual isolation valve handle. This will keep hydraulic pressure on the stow side of the actuators during the flex shaft installation. 1) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00.

H. Sync Shaft Installation

SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-005-F00 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHES AND GLOVES WHEN YOU DO WORK ON THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE A LEAK FROM THE OPEN PORTS OF THE COMPONENT OR FROM THE HYDRAULIC LINES. INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT LET HYDRAULIC FLUID GET ON THE THRUST REVERSER OR ENGINE COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN A COMPONENT IF HYDRAULIC FLUID GETS ON IT . HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT . (1) Do these steps to install the sync shaft [4] and tube [2] or tube [3]: CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO LOOSEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUT . USE ONE TO HOLD THE FITTING, AND THE OTHER TO LOOSEN THE COUPLING NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) Remove the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3] that was temporarily installed. 1) Replace the two O-rings [31] and four backup rings [30] on the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3]. a) Slide the coupling nut and tube adapter away from the end of the tube. b) Remove and discard the two O-rings [31] and four backup rings [30]. c) Clean the seal surfaces and grooves with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with solvent, B00316. <1> Wipe all the solvent off the surfaces with a clean, dry cloth. NOTE: Do not let the solvent dry on the surfaces. d) Lubricate the two new O-rings [31] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153. e) Install the two O-rings [31] and four new backup rings [30]. NOTE: An O-ring is installed with two backup rings. There is a backup ring on each side of the O-ring. 78-31-04 f) Slide the coupling nut and tube adapter toward the end of the tube [2] or tube [3]. CAUTION DO NOT LET DIRT OR OTHER CONTAMINATION GET ON THE SYNC SHAFT . DAMAGE TO THE SYNC SHAFT CAN OCCUR. (b) If there is contamination on the sync shaft [4], remove the contamination with a cotton wiper, G00034. (c) Insert the sync shaft [4] into the tube [2] or tube [3]. (d) Move the coupling nuts and tube adapters back along the tube to get access to the sync shaft ends. (e) Insert one end of the sync shaft [4] into the internal spline in the actuator port [1]. (f) Flex the sync shaft [4] and insert the opposite end into the internal spline in the other actuator port [1]. (g) Tighten the coupling nuts enough to engage one or two threads at this time. (h) Center the tube [2] or tube [3] in the coupling nuts and adapters. CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO TIGHTEN THE COUPLING NUT . USE ONE TO HOLD THE FITTING, AND THE OTHER TO TURN THE COUPLING NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (i) Do these steps to tighten the coupling nuts: 1) Tighten the coupling nut to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m). 2) Loosen the coupling nut. 3) Tighten the coupling nut again to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m). SUBTASK 78-31-04-410-001-F00 (2) To install the clampblocks, do these steps: NOTE: To eliminate tubing preload, it is important to install the clampblock retainer, clampblock, and spacers back in their original positions. (a) For the upper clampblock, install the two bolts [9], two washers [10], clampblock retainer [8], and clampblock [11]. (b) For the lower clampblock, install the two bolts [16], two washers [17], clampblock retainer [15], and clampblock [18]. (c) Tighten the bolts [9] and bolts [16] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m). SUBTASK 78-31-04-040-004-F00 (3) Do these steps again: (a) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. (b) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. 78-31-04 WARNING DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE TO PREVENT THE OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSER. THE ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSER CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (c) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00. (d) For Engine 1, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 7 C01266 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK (e) For Engine 2, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01267 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-007-F00 (4) Move the applicable reverse thrust lever forward and down to the retract (stow) position. SUBTASK 78-31-04-080-001-F00 (5) Do these steps to disconnect the thrust reverser maintenance lock equipment, SPL-9002, B78009-5 cable assembly, from the control valve module: (a) Disconnect the P1 connector of the -5 cable assembly from the control valve module receptacle. (b) Disconnect the electrical connector from the J1 receptacle of the -5 cable assembly. (c) Connect the electrical connector to the control valve module. 1) For Engine 1, connect the electrical connector, D03052. 2) For Engine 2, connect the electrical connector, D03056. SUBTASK 78-31-04-980-001-F00 (6) Manually extend and retract the thrust reverser through one cycle. (a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00. (b) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Manual Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-804-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-008-F00 (7) For Engine 1, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 5 C00276 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER CONT B 7 C01266 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-009-F00 (8) For Engine 2, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01267 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER SYNC LOCK 78-31-04 (Continued) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 7 C00277 ENGINE 2 THRUST REVERSER CONT SUBTASK 78-31-04-440-001-F00 (9) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-710-001-F00 (10) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Normal Operation Test, TASK 78-31-00-700-801-F00. (a) Remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag from the reverse thrust lever. (b) Operate the thrust reverser through the extend (deploy) and retract (stow) cycles at least 3 times until all of the air is removed from the thrust reverser hydraulic system. NOTE: This is shown by a smooth movement of the sleeves. 1) Do a check of the hydraulic tubes and connections for hydraulic fluid leaks. a) If you find leaks, do this task: Hydraulic System External Leakage Check, TASK 29-00-00-790-801. NOTE: Refer to the Tube Connections, Static Seals, and Other Dynamic Seals sections of the procedure for the leakage limits.

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 78-31-04-410-003-F00 (1) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.

78-31-04-200-801-F00Sync Shaft - Inspection/Check ATA 78 · Task 200-801-F00

Task Description

2. Sync Shaft - Inspection/Check (Figure 601)

A. References

Reference Title 78-31-04-000-801-F00 Sync Shaft Removal (P/B 401) 78-31-04-400-801-F00 Sync Shaft Installation (P/B 401)

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-3912 Lens - Magnifying, 5x, Hand Held

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 415 Engine 1 - Thrust Reverser, Left 416 Engine 1 - Thrust Reverser, Right 425 Engine 2 - Thrust Reverser, Left 426 Engine 2 - Thrust Reverser, Right

D. Inspection the Sync Shaft

SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-005-F00 (1) Examine the sync shaft tubes for evidence of hydraulic fluid leaks. (a) Tighten or replace sync shafts as necessary to stop any leaks that are found. NOTE: If a leak is found in the lower sync shaft P/N 315A1825–25, replace the tube with P/N 315A1805–29 or refer to Service Letter 737–SL-78–057–A. SUBTASK 78-31-04-020-003-F00 (2) For the applicable sync shaft, do this task: Sync Shaft Removal, TASK 78-31-04-000-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-001-F00 (3) Use a hand held 5x magnifying lens, STD-3912 to do a visual inspection of the sync shaft wires: (a) Look for a broken wire. 1) If you find a broken wire, then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00. (b) Look for wire strand separations. 1) If the width of the strand separation is equal to or less than the diameter of the wire strand, then the sync shaft is acceptable. 2) If the width of the strand separation is greater than the diameter of the wire strand, then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-002-F00 (4) Look for twists in the square ends of the sync shaft. 78-31-04 (a) If you find a twist in the square end, then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-003-F00 (5) Look for kinks in the sync shaft. (a) If you find a kink that is less than or equal to 0.020 inch (0.508 mm), then the sync shaft is acceptable. (b) If you find a kink that is greater than 0.020 inch (0.508 mm), then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-004-F00 (6) Look for abraded or worn areas on the surface of the sync shaft. (a) If you find abraded or worn areas, then calculate the amount of face wear W: 1) Measure the diameter D2 of the sync shaft at the maximum depth of the worn area. 2) Measure the diameter D1 of the sync shaft in an adjacent area that is not damaged. 3) Subtract diameter D2 from diameter D1 and then divide by 2. NOTE: (D1 - D2) /2 = W. (b) If the face wear W is less than or equal to 0.013 inch (0.330 mm), then the sync shaft is acceptable. (c) If the face wear W is greater than 0.013 inch (0.330 mm), then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-007-F00 (7) If the sync shaft is serviceable, do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00.
